title: A meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease
methods: regional meta-analysis of FA and MD
main finding: AD showed widespread lower FA and higher MD; MCI effects were already present but less extensive
relevance_to_current_claim: Any claim that FA or MD separates CN, MCI and AD must be framed as replication or refinement
limitations: Substantial acquisition and analysis heterogeneity; mainly clinically defined groups

title: New MRI Markers for Alzheimer's Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Diffusion Tensor Imaging and a Comparison with Medial Temporal Lobe Measurements
cohort: 55 DTI studies with 2791 participants; 76 medial temporal atrophy studies with 8122 participants
main finding: DTI abnormalities were widespread and complementary to medial temporal atrophy
relevance_to_current_claim: DTI-only differentiation is mature literature and not a novel premise
limitations: Study-level heterogeneity and mostly cross-sectional clinical diagnosis

title: Diffusion tensor imaging of white matter degeneration in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment
methods: review of ROI, voxelwise and tract-based findings
main finding: Convergent damage involves limbic and late-myelinating association pathways but metric interpretation is nonspecific
relevance_to_current_claim: Supports a multilevel story while warning against calling FA integrity
limitations: Narrative rather than quantitative synthesis

title: Graph Theory and Brain Connectivity in Alzheimer's Disease
main finding: AD is consistently framed as a network-disconnection disorder, with hub and efficiency abnormalities
relevance_to_current_claim: Generic graph disruption is not novel
limitations: Mixed modalities and heterogeneous graph construction

title: Imaging Alzheimer's genetic risk using diffusion MRI: A systematic review
methods: systematic synthesis of APOE and polygenic-risk studies
main finding: Genetic risk is associated with subtle, spatially heterogeneous diffusion differences before dementia
relevance_to_current_claim: APOE or genetic moderation is already a substantial literature
limitations: Small heterogeneous studies and inconsistent diffusion models

title: Machine Learning for the Classification of Alzheimer's Disease and Its Prodromal Stage Using Brain Diffusion Tensor Imaging Data: A Systematic Review
methods: review of feature engineering, classifiers and validation
main finding: Many high reported accuracies were based on small cohorts and heterogeneous validation
relevance_to_current_claim: A classifier alone, even if accurate internally, is not a biological novelty claim
limitations: Quality of included evidence varied; external validation uncommon

title: The human connectome in Alzheimer disease — relationship to biomarkers and genetics
methods: mechanistic review of hubs, pathology spread and biomarkers
main finding: Amyloid preferentially involves hubs and tau spread is constrained by connectivity; connectome models link pathology to progression
relevance_to_current_claim: Pathology-connectome-cognition framing is established; novelty must be an exact conditional or longitudinal result
limitations: Review integrates structural and functional evidence, not all subject-specific dMRI

title: Abnormal white matter changes in Alzheimer's disease based on diffusion tensor imaging: A systematic review
cohort: multilevel DTI studies across SCD, MCI and AD
methods: voxelwise, tractwise, networkwise and classification synthesis
main finding: Corpus callosum, fornix, medial temporal lobe, hippocampus and cingulum recur across levels
relevance_to_current_claim: Limbic involvement and stage gradients cannot be claimed as new
limitations: Reported classification values inherit primary-study leakage and cohort limitations

title: Topologically convergent and divergent large scale complex networks among Alzheimer's disease spectrum patients: A systematic review
main finding: Convergent deficits center on the default-mode network, while modality-specific neighboring changes diverge
relevance_to_current_claim: A broad DMN or topology claim is saturated
limitations: Combines dMRI, morphometric covariance and functional networks; methods are not interchangeable

title: Disentangling in-vivo microstructural changes of white and gray matter in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
methods: meta-analysis of NDI, ODI and isotropic fraction
main finding: NODDI abnormalities recur in cingulum, uncinate, posterior thalamic radiation, superior longitudinal fasciculus and hippocampal regions
relevance_to_current_claim: NODDI sensitivity is prior art; an exact network-level integration may still be testable
limitations: Only ten heterogeneous studies; limited longitudinal evidence

title: The whole-brain structural and functional connectome in Alzheimer's disease spectrum: A multimodal Bayesian meta-analysis of graph theoretical characteristics
methods: Bayesian meta-analysis of global graph metrics
main finding: AD showed lower structural integration and segregation; preclinical AD also showed reduced integration
relevance_to_current_claim: Global efficiency, path length, clustering and local efficiency are no longer candidate novelty claims
limitations: Only metrics reported often enough could be pooled; graph pipelines remained heterogeneous

title: The Role of Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy, Diffusion-Tensor-Imaging and Structural MRI in Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Diagnosis: A Review
main finding: DTI contributes complementary microstructural information but requires multimodal and longitudinal validation
relevance_to_current_claim: Supports positioning diffusion as one layer rather than a standalone diagnostic truth
limitations: Very recent review; not a quantitative absence test

title: Diffusion tensor imaging of cingulum fibers in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer disease
main finding: Cingulum FA showed a CN to MCI to AD gradient; combining DTI with hippocampal volume improved discrimination
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art against a novel cingulum or limbic-FA claim
limitations: Small sample and ROI selection; clinical rather than biomarker definition

title: Regionally-specific diffusion tensor imaging in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease
cohort: CN, MCI and AD clinical groups
main finding: Regional diffusion abnormalities differentiated MCI and AD and related to cognition
relevance_to_current_claim: Regional DTI stage effects are established
limitations: Cross-sectional and susceptible to partial volume

title: Absolute diffusivities define the landscape of white matter degeneration in Alzheimer's disease
methods: whole-brain TBSS of FA, MD, axial and radial diffusivity
main finding: Absolute diffusivities were more widespread than FA, especially in fornix, cingulum and temporoparietal pathways
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for MD, RD and axial diffusivity being more sensitive than FA
limitations: Tensor metrics remain biologically nonspecific and crossing-fiber sensitive

title: Longitudinal changes in fiber tract integrity in healthy aging and mild cognitive impairment: a DTI follow-up study
main finding: MCI showed tract-specific longitudinal diffusion changes beyond healthy aging
relevance_to_current_claim: Longitudinal DTI change is established
limitations: Modest sample and older acquisition

title: Diffusion tensor imaging and tract-based spatial statistics in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment
main finding: Widespread tract abnormalities were greatest in AD with MCI intermediate
relevance_to_current_claim: A monotonic CN-MCI-AD diffusion gradient is not novel
limitations: Small single-site cohort and cross-sectional inference

title: DTI measures in crossing-fibre areas: increased diffusion anisotropy reveals early white matter alteration in MCI and mild Alzheimer's disease
main finding: Some regions showed paradoxically increased FA because degeneration of one crossing population unmasks another
relevance_to_current_claim: Critical warning that FA direction is not a simple integrity scale
limitations: Tensor model cannot resolve the underlying fiber populations directly

title: The fornix sign: a potential sign for Alzheimer's disease based on diffusion tensor imaging
methods: visual and quantitative fornix FA sign
main finding: The fornix sign predicted CN-to-aMCI and aMCI-to-AD conversion in a small cohort
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for fornix-based prognosis
limitations: Small sample and optimistic single-cohort diagnostic estimates

title: Longitudinal, region-specific course of diffusion tensor imaging measures in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease
methods: generalized estimating equations for regional FA and MD
main finding: Fornix and splenium differences were stable and some changes emerged during MCI
relevance_to_current_claim: Regional longitudinal DTI trajectories are established
limitations: Regional sampling and limited power for conversion subgroups

title: Brain microstructure reveals early abnormalities more than two years prior to clinical progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease
main finding: Diffusion abnormalities preceded clinical conversion by more than two years
relevance_to_current_claim: Preconversion diffusion signal is established prior art
limitations: Clinical conversion endpoint and modest cohort

title: Widespread white matter degeneration preceding the onset of dementia
main finding: Free-water-corrected radial diffusivity was widespread in MCI converters but not stable MCI
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for conversion-sensitive advanced DTI
limitations: Small cohort and no external validation

title: White-matter integrity on DTI and the pathologic staging of Alzheimer's disease
methods: DTI associations with Braak and amyloid plaque stages
main finding: Limbic and medial parietal DTI abnormalities tracked tau stage and severity more than amyloid plaques
relevance_to_current_claim: Strong prior art for limbic diffusion-tau linkage
limitations: Antemortem-to-autopsy interval and selected autopsy cohort

title: Dissociable diffusion MRI patterns of white matter microstructure and connectivity in Alzheimer's disease spectrum
methods: linked independent-component analysis across FA, MD, RD, axial diffusivity, crossing-fiber and connectivity-density measures
main finding: Coordinated but dissociable microstructural and connectivity patterns followed disease severity
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for integrating diffusion scalars with connectivity into one story
limitations: Clinical groups, cross-sectional design and no external replication

title: 3D tract-specific local and global analysis of white matter integrity in Alzheimer's disease
main finding: Tract-specific abnormalities showed a graded CN-MCI-AD pattern
relevance_to_current_claim: Along-tract differentiation is established
limitations: ADNI cohort reuse and tensor-model limitations

title: Individual classification of Alzheimer's disease with diffusion magnetic resonance imaging
methods: ICA features, raw connectomes and graph measures with classification
main finding: FA independent components and raw connectomes achieved higher AUC than many summary graph metrics
relevance_to_current_claim: Diffusion-connectome classification is not novel by itself
limitations: AD versus control only; internal validation and cohort effects

title: Distinct white matter microstructural abnormalities and extracellular water increases relate to cognitive impairment in Alzheimer's disease with and without cerebrovascular disease
cohort: AD with and without cerebrovascular disease, vascular dementia and controls
main finding: Extracellular water and tissue changes differed across AD and vascular disease and related to cognition
relevance_to_current_claim: Vascular and free-water confounding must be modeled before attributing effects to AD
limitations: Cross-sectional clinical groups and indirect biological interpretation

title: Fibre-specific white matter reductions in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment
main finding: AD showed widespread fiber-specific loss; MCI effects were more focal and amyloid stratification complicated the pattern
relevance_to_current_claim: Fixel analysis and posterior cingulum findings are established
limitations: Cross-sectional and some MCI effects were driven by amyloid-negative cases

title: Microstructural White Matter Alterations in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease: Study Based on NODDI
main finding: NDI, ODI and isotropic fraction detected MCI changes not seen with FA
relevance_to_current_claim: NODDI sensitivity over FA is established
limitations: Very small sample and no external validation

title: Free Water in White Matter Differentiates MCI and AD From Control Subjects
main finding: MCI and AD had higher free water even after excluding WMH and partial-volume-prone regions
relevance_to_current_claim: Free-water differentiation is established
limitations: Cross-sectional ADNI analysis; free water is not a direct neuroinflammation assay

title: White matter alterations in early-stage Alzheimer's disease: A tract-specific study
journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring
main finding: Different diffusion models captured complementary tract abnormalities in early disease
relevance_to_current_claim: Multimetric tract analysis is established
limitations: Exploratory feature set and limited sample

title: Specific White Matter Tracts and Diffusion Properties Predict Conversion From Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease
main finding: Axial diffusivity in right hippocampal cingulum, right IFOF and left ILF helped predict conversion; FA was near chance
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for tract-level conversion prediction and axial diffusivity superiority
limitations: Accuracy about 0.75, single cohort and no biomarker confirmation

title: Comparative Evaluation of Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging and Diffusion Tensor Imaging in Detecting Cerebral Microstructural Changes in Alzheimer Disease
main finding: Both DKI and DTI detected abnormalities; DKI changes were more spatially limited
relevance_to_current_claim: DKI is not automatically more sensitive or specific than DTI
limitations: Small binary cohort and no MCI group

title: Diffusion models reveal white matter microstructural changes with ageing, pathology and cognition
cohort: older adults spanning pathology and cognitive status
methods: comparison of tensor and advanced diffusion models
main finding: Metrics showed spatially heterogeneous associations with age, pathology and cognition
relevance_to_current_claim: Supports complementary rather than interchangeable diffusion metrics
limitations: Observational associations and multiple models increase multiplicity

title: Microstructural white matter alterations in Alzheimer's disease and amnestic mild cognitive impairment and its diagnostic value based on diffusion kurtosis imaging
methods: TBSS, cognition correlations and ROC analysis
main finding: Kurtosis FA was altered in aMCI and splenial KFA had strong diagnostic performance
relevance_to_current_claim: DKI-based early differentiation is established
limitations: Single site and no independent test cohort

title: Greater Diffusion Restriction in White Matter in Preclinical Alzheimer Disease
cohort: cognitively unimpaired amyloid-negative and amyloid-positive adults
main finding: Amyloid positivity was associated with a complex pattern including greater restriction consistent with early reactive processes
relevance_to_current_claim: Direction of diffusion change can be biphasic, not simply degeneration
limitations: Cross-sectional mechanistic interpretation; preclinical stage only

title: Diffusion tensor tractography of the fornix in cerebral amyloid angiopathy, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease
main finding: Fornix diffusivity was greatest in AD and CAA, while MCI did not differ from controls; tract volume was lower across clinical groups
relevance_to_current_claim: Fornix findings are neither AD-specific nor uniformly present in MCI
limitations: Two centers and clinical diagnoses; residual partial volume possible

title: Investigating Tissue-Specific Abnormalities in Alzheimer's Disease with Multi-Shell Diffusion MRI
methods: multi-tissue CSD with fixel, voxel and tensor morphometry
main finding: Fiber-specific and tissue-composition abnormalities extended beyond conventional DTI findings
relevance_to_current_claim: Tissue-specific multilevel diffusion analysis is established
limitations: Cross-sectional and modest cohort; no external replication

title: Disentangling the effects of Alzheimer's and small vessel disease on white matter fibre tracts
cohort: 387 participants including biomarker-defined AD and cerebral small-vessel disease
main finding: AD and small-vessel disease produced distinguishable fiber-specific patterns
relevance_to_current_claim: Any AD claim must account for vascular burden rather than treat all white-matter change as AD
limitations: Observational group contrasts and disease comorbidity remain complex

title: White Matter Degeneration Pathways Associated With Tau Deposition in Alzheimer Disease
cohort: amyloid-positive adults from MCSA and ADRC
modality: NODDI, amyloid PET and tau PET
main finding: Tau deposition related to NODDI abnormalities in connected temporal and cingulum pathways and to cognition
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for tau-linked tract microstructure
limitations: Cross-sectional imaging cannot establish propagation direction

title: Fixel-Based Analysis Reveals Tau-Related White Matter Changes in Early Stages of Alzheimer's Disease
methods: fixel-based FD, FC and FDC with DTI comparison
main finding: Macrostructural fiber cross-section was related to tau and memory; DTI effects were broader but less pathology-specific
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for tau-fixel-cognition linkage
limitations: Cross-sectional mediation cannot prove causality

title: White matter alterations and their associations with biomarkers and behavior in subjective cognitive decline individuals: a fixel-based analysis
journal: Fluids and Barriers of the CNS
main finding: Fiber-specific changes in SCD related to biomarker and behavioral measures
relevance_to_current_claim: Fixel abnormalities before MCI are prior art
limitations: SCD is etiologically heterogeneous and cross-sectional

title: NODDI-derived measures of microstructural integrity in medial temporal lobe white matter pathways are associated with Alzheimer's disease pathology and cognition
cohort: 199 ADNI3 participants; tau PET n=135; amyloid PET n=146
methods: medial-temporal tract ROI, mediation and random forest
main finding: NDI and ODI related more strongly than FA to tau, amyloid and memory; NDI partially mediated pathology-memory associations
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for limbic NODDI-pathology-cognition integration
limitations: Only 12 dementia cases; cross-sectional mediation and ADNI reuse

title: Mapping Alzheimer's disease pathology using free water through integrated analysis of plasma biomarkers, microstructural DTI metrics, and macrostructural MRI measures
modality: free-water DTI, structural MRI and plasma p-tau217
main finding: Plasma p-tau217 related to free water but not FA or MD; free water had direct and indirect cognitive associations
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for plasma-pathology to diffusion to cognition integration
limitations: Single health-system cohort and observational mediation

title: Structure–function coupling using fixel-based analysis and functional magnetic resonance imaging in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment
methods: fixel-based structural connectome and structure-function coupling
main finding: Fixel-based structural connectivity revealed stage-related coupling alterations and cognitive associations
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for combining fixels, connectomes and function
limitations: ADNI reuse, cross-sectional analysis and published erratum

title: Analysis of advanced diffusion models assessing white matter microstructure in Alzheimer's disease
main finding: Advanced diffusion models identified complementary widespread abnormalities
relevance_to_current_claim: Simply adding advanced diffusion models is no longer methodologically novel
limitations: Single-center cross-sectional study without external validation

title: Diffusion Tensor Tractography Reveals Abnormal Topological Organization in Structural Cortical Networks in Alzheimer's Disease
main finding: AD had longer shortest paths, lower global efficiency and frontal nodal-efficiency abnormalities while retaining small-world organization
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for integration loss and path-length claims
limitations: Small cohort, deterministic tensor tractography and density sensitivity

title: Disrupted topological organization in white matter structural networks in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: relationship to subtype
main finding: Global topology was more disrupted in multidomain than single-domain aMCI and related to cognition
relevance_to_current_claim: MCI subtype and topology effects are established
limitations: Small clinically defined subgroups and cross-sectional staging

title: Prediction of Alzheimer's disease using individual structural connectivity networks
main finding: Individual structural networks distinguished AD and predementia cases from controls with high internal accuracy
relevance_to_current_claim: Connectome-based individual diagnosis and prognosis predate modern GNNs
limitations: Small cohort and likely optimistic internal validation

title: Breakdown of Brain Connectivity Between Normal Aging and Alzheimer's Disease: A Structural k-Core Network Analysis
main finding: Progressive loss involved network shells and core organization across the disease continuum
relevance_to_current_claim: Core-periphery progression is established prior art
limitations: Threshold and tractography choices influence k-core membership

title: Disruption of cerebral networks and cognitive impairment in Alzheimer disease
methods: whole-brain graph metrics with cognitive regression
main finding: Lower local efficiency related to memory and executive deficits and added explanatory variance beyond atrophy and small-vessel markers
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for topology-cognition relationships
limitations: Small control group and observational regression

title: Alzheimer's Disease Disrupts Rich Club Organization in Brain Connectivity Networks
main finding: AD had lower degree yet a higher normalized rich-club coefficient at some thresholds because edge loss changed normalization
relevance_to_current_claim: A directionally higher rich-club coefficient can be a density artifact, not compensation
limitations: Short conference paper and threshold-dependent metric

title: The Alzheimer Structural Connectome: Changes in Cortical Network Topology with Increased Amyloid Plaque Burden
cohort: 102 ADNI2 participants with DTI and florbetapir PET
modality: DTI tractography, amyloid PET and structural MRI
methods: regional graph topology and amyloid associations
main finding: Structural topology differed across CN, MCI and AD and related to amyloid burden
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for amyloid-connectome topology
limitations: Cross-sectional ADNI snapshot and regional multiple testing

title: Rich Club Analysis in the Alzheimer's Disease Connectome Reveals a Relatively Undisturbed Structural Core Network
methods: rich-club, feeder and peripheral edge analysis
main finding: Disease effects were often greater in lower-degree and peripheral connections than in the structural core
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art against a simple selective hub-vulnerability story
limitations: Rich-club definition, thresholding and ADNI cohort reuse

title: Brain connectivity and novel network measures for Alzheimer's disease classification
cohort: 200 ADNI participants: 50 CN, 74 early MCI, 38 late MCI, 38 AD
main finding: Structural connectivity and novel graph features supported multistage classification
relevance_to_current_claim: Graph-feature machine learning on ADNI is established
limitations: Proof-of-concept internal cross-validation and cohort reuse

title: Global Efficiency of Structural Networks Mediates Cognitive Control in Mild Cognitive Impairment
methods: tract microstructure, global graph topology and mediation
main finding: Reduced global efficiency and clustering partly mediated cingulum-microstructure associations with cognitive control
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for tract-to-topology-to-cognition mediation
limitations: Cross-sectional mediation does not prove causal sequence

title: Stability of graph theoretical measures in structural brain networks in Alzheimer's disease
methods: graph stability across thresholds and subsamples
main finding: Graph conclusions varied with construction choices; some measures were more stable than others
relevance_to_current_claim: A robustness audit is required before treating a dashboard metric as biological
limitations: Uses morphometric covariance rather than subject-level dMRI connectomes

title: Rich club disturbances of the human connectome from subjective cognitive decline to Alzheimer's disease
methods: rich-club, feeder and local connection analysis
main finding: Peripheral and feeder connections were affected earlier, with rich-club connections more involved in aMCI and AD
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for stage-dependent core-periphery progression
limitations: Clinical staging, age differences and cross-sectional inference

title: Distinct Patterns of Rich Club Organization in Alzheimer's Disease and Subcortical Vascular Dementia: A White Matter Network Study
cohort: 30 amyloid-positive AD, 39 amyloid-negative subcortical vascular dementia, 72 CN
main finding: AD and vascular dementia showed different rich-club disruption patterns
relevance_to_current_claim: Vascular disease can mimic but reorganize networks differently; vascular adjustment is essential
limitations: Cross-sectional and diagnosis-specific sampling

title: Metastable neural dynamics in Alzheimer's disease are disrupted by lesions to the structural connectome
modality: dMRI structural connectome and resting-state fMRI
methods: subject-specific network lesioning and dynamical modeling
main finding: Structural lesions around hubs and default-mode regions reduced simulated metastability and related to cognition
relevance_to_current_claim: Network dynamics provides a prior mechanistic bridge beyond graph summaries
limitations: Causal language is model-based; lesion definition included liberal tractwise thresholds

title: Changes in functional and structural brain connectome along the Alzheimer's disease continuum
cohort: controls, stable aMCI, converter aMCI and AD
modality: dMRI, resting-state fMRI and structural MRI
methods: structural and functional graph analysis with conversion groups
main finding: Connectome disruption differed across stable and converter MCI and related to the distribution of atrophy
relevance_to_current_claim: Multimodal continuum and conversion analysis is established
limitations: Multiple modalities and cohort stratification reduce effective power

title: Identifying Brain Connectivity Using Network-Based Statistics in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment Stratified by β-Amyloid Positivity
journal: American Journal of Alzheimer's Disease & Other Dementias
cohort: 35 amyloid-negative CN, 42 amyloid-negative aMCI, 39 amyloid-positive aMCI
main finding: Amyloid-positive aMCI showed medial frontal disruption, but no NBS component separated amyloid-positive from amyloid-negative aMCI
relevance_to_current_claim: NBS and amyloid-stratified MCI are prior art; null contrasts also matter
limitations: Small clinical groups, deterministic DTI and threshold dependence

title: Communicability disruption in Alzheimer's disease connectivity networks
main finding: Communicability captured distributed loss beyond shortest paths in AD and converter MCI
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for a communicability-based claim
limitations: Single cohort and graph construction sensitivity

title: Prediction of Conversion From Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease Based on the Brain Structural Connectome
cohort: 52 aMCI and 26 controls; converters versus non-converters
main finding: Default-mode structural disruption was more severe in converters; internal converter classification reached about 81 percent
relevance_to_current_claim: Conversion prediction from topology is established prior art
limitations: Small converter sample and no external validation

title: Connectome-wide network analysis of white matter connectivity in Alzheimer's disease
cohort: 161 CN, stable MCI, converter MCI and AD
methods: multivariate distance-matrix regression and discriminant analysis
main finding: Disease-related seed networks expanded with severity; nine regions distinguished CN, converter MCI and AD
relevance_to_current_claim: Connectome-wide edge signatures and limbic-subcortical findings are established
limitations: Cross-sectional baseline with modest subgroups and internal discrimination

title: Multiparametric graph theoretical analysis reveals altered structural and functional network topology in Alzheimer's disease
methods: FA, streamline count, inverse diffusivity and functional edge definitions
main finding: Limbic, prefrontal and occipital topology varied by edge definition; tract diffusivities were often more interpretable than counts
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for integrating FA, MD, RD, axial diffusivity and graph metrics
limitations: Small single-site cohort; age and education differed among groups

title: Disrupted structural and functional brain networks in Alzheimer's disease
main finding: AD showed related but nonidentical structural and functional network disruption
relevance_to_current_claim: An SC-FC story is established and should not conflate modalities
limitations: Cross-sectional and modality-specific preprocessing choices

title: Effects of Brain Parcellation on the Characterization of Topological Deterioration in Alzheimer's Disease
main finding: Which graph measures separated groups changed materially across parcellations
relevance_to_current_claim: Any proposed signature requires cross-atlas sensitivity analysis
limitations: ADNI-only and a limited atlas set

title: Abnormal Anatomical Rich-Club Organization and Structural–Functional Coupling in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease
main finding: Rich-club organization and coupling were abnormal across MCI and AD
relevance_to_current_claim: Rich-club plus SC-FC coupling is established prior art
limitations: Cross-sectional and sensitive to hub and threshold definitions

title: Compensatory Brain Connection Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease
cohort: public dMRI cohorts with replication databases
main finding: Anti-correlated connections were proposed as compensatory pathways and validated across datasets
relevance_to_current_claim: A generic compensation claim from inverse edge correlations is prior art
limitations: Correlation is not neural compensation; conference-length report

title: Disrupted Network Topology Contributed to Spatial Navigation Impairment in Patients With Mild Cognitive Impairment
main finding: Topology disruption related to spatial-navigation impairment in MCI
relevance_to_current_claim: Specific cognitive-domain links beyond memory are already studied
limitations: Cross-sectional and clinically defined MCI

title: Combined Support Vector Machine Classifier and Brain Structural Network Features for the Individual Classification of Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment and Subjective Cognitive Decline Patients
methods: multi-kernel SVM using fiber-number, FA and MD connectomes
main finding: Combining edge definitions differentiated SCD and aMCI; MD-weighted frontal connections were informative
relevance_to_current_claim: Multikernel classification across FN, FA and MD is established
limitations: Single cohort and internal validation only

title: Consistency of Graph Theoretical Measurements of Alzheimer's Disease Fiber Density Connectomes Across Multiple Parcellation Scales
main finding: Transitivity was most consistent; characteristic path length was highly scale-sensitive
relevance_to_current_claim: Cross-scale replication is mandatory for topology claims
limitations: Conference paper, ADNI-only and four global metrics

title: Sex differences in the structural rich-club connectivity in patients with Alzheimer's disease
cohort: 260 amyloid-negative CN, 281 prodromal AD, 285 AD dementia
modality: DTI, structural MRI and amyloid PET
main finding: Women with AD showed lower rich-club and feeder connectivity than men
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for a sex-specific rich-club claim
limitations: Cross-sectional and potential residual sex-related anatomy and scanner effects

title: Structural Network Topology Reveals Higher Brain Resilience in Individuals with Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease
cohort: 68 cognitively normal: A-T-, A+T- and A+T+
modality: dMRI, amyloid PET and tau PET
main finding: A+T+ cognitively normal participants showed higher assortativity without a global-efficiency difference, interpreted as resilience
relevance_to_current_claim: Preclinical compensatory or resilient topology is already a candidate framework
limitations: Small pathology strata and cross-sectional interpretation

title: Multimodal imaging investigation of structural rich club alterations in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Amyloid deposition, structural atrophy, and functional activation differences
modality: dMRI, longitudinal structural MRI, amyloid PET and meta-analytic function
main finding: Rich-club regions showed accelerated atrophy and increased amyloid in MCI and AD
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for multimodal hub vulnerability
limitations: Some functional evidence was meta-analytic rather than subject-specific

title: A novel method for PET connectomics guided by fibre-tracking MRI: Application to Alzheimer's disease
cohort: ADNI HC, EMCI, LMCI and AD
modality: tau PET, dMRI and T1 MRI
methods: SIFT2 structural connectome, track-weighted PET and NBS
main finding: Structural connectivity decreased from LMCI onward while tau-weighted connectivity increased from EMCI; limbic edges recurred
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for SIFT2 plus tau-PET edge weighting and NBS
limitations: Novel edge measure needs independent biological validation; ADNI reuse

title: Structural white matter connectivity differences independent of gray matter loss in mild cognitive impairment with neuropsychiatric symptoms: Early indicators of Alzheimer's disease using network-based statistics
cohort: ADNI MCI with and without neuropsychiatric symptoms
main finding: White-matter subnetworks differed with neuropsychiatric symptoms independently of gray-matter loss
relevance_to_current_claim: NBS subnetwork claims must be specific because symptom-stratified work exists
limitations: Cross-sectional ADNI analysis and primary-threshold dependence

title: Integrating individualized connectome with amyloid pathology improves predictive modeling of future cognitive decline
cohort: 77 discovery participants and 72 ADNI3 external participants
modality: subject-specific dMRI connectome, amyloid PET, tau PET and cognition
methods: connectome-informed pathology features with repeated cross-validation and external testing
main finding: Individual structural-connectome-weighted amyloid improved prediction of future cognition and partially generalized across cohorts
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for individualized connectome plus amyloid plus external prediction
limitations: Small cohorts, some outcomes failed external validation and no multiplicity correction for selected follow-ups

title: Complex network measures of brain connectivity: Uses and interpretations
methods: definitions and interpretation of graph measures
main finding: Established how segregation, integration, centrality and resilience measures should be interpreted
relevance_to_current_claim: Required foundation for any graph-theory claim
limitations: Generic framework rather than an AD-specific validation

title: Network-based statistic: Identifying differences in brain networks
main finding: NBS controls component-level family-wise error while exploiting connected effects
relevance_to_current_claim: Critical for interpreting significant subnetworks; significance attaches to the component, not each edge
limitations: Inference depends on the chosen primary threshold and does not localize individually significant edges

title: Comparing brain networks of different size and connectivity density using graph theory
main finding: Many graph metrics change systematically with network size and density
relevance_to_current_claim: Density-matched or cost-integrated sensitivity analysis is required
limitations: Does not prescribe one universally optimal normalization

title: Anatomically constrained tractography: Improved diffusion MRI streamlines tractography through effective use of anatomical information
main finding: Anatomical tissue constraints reduce biologically implausible streamline trajectories
relevance_to_current_claim: MRtrix ACT is established methodology and not a biological novelty
limitations: Accuracy still depends on registration, segmentation and tractography parameters

title: A network diffusion model of disease progression in dementia
cohort: patient atrophy data with a healthy structural-connectome template
modality: structural MRI and normative dMRI connectome
main finding: A simple diffusion process on the structural network reproduced characteristic regional atrophy patterns
relevance_to_current_claim: Network-mediated AD spread has been formalized for more than a decade
limitations: Template connectome and regional atrophy cannot demonstrate individual axonal propagation

title: White matter integrity, fiber count, and other fallacies: The do's and don'ts of diffusion MRI
main finding: FA, MD, streamline count and related measures are nonspecific and can reflect multiple tissue or modeling factors
relevance_to_current_claim: Prevents mechanistic over-interpretation of FA or streamline-weight changes
limitations: Conceptual guidance rather than a complete generative tissue model

title: Spurious group differences due to head motion in a diffusion MRI study
main finding: Residual head-motion differences can create apparent diffusion group effects
relevance_to_current_claim: Motion summaries and sensitivity analyses are mandatory in CN-MCI-AD comparisons
limitations: Correction procedures and acquisition technology have evolved since publication

title: Anatomical accuracy of brain connections derived from diffusion MRI tractography is inherently limited
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
main finding: Diffusion tractography showed fundamental limits in recovering true anatomical connectivity
relevance_to_current_claim: A connectome edge is an algorithm-dependent estimate, not a verified axonal connection
limitations: Nonhuman ex vivo benchmark and tractography methods continue to improve

title: Multi-tissue constrained spherical deconvolution for improved analysis of multi-shell diffusion MRI data
main finding: Separating tissue response functions improves fiber-orientation estimation in partial-volume regions
relevance_to_current_claim: Advanced CSD is established pipeline methodology
limitations: Requires suitable acquisition and accurate response-function estimation

title: SIFT2: Enabling dense quantitative assessment of brain white matter connectivity using streamlines tractography
main finding: Per-streamline weights improve agreement between tractography and fiber-density information
relevance_to_current_claim: SIFT2-weighted connectomes are established and are not intrinsically quantitative axon counts
limitations: Weights remain model dependent and do not solve all false-positive tractography

title: Overcoming the effects of false positives and threshold bias in graph theoretical analyses of neuroimaging data
main finding: False positives and threshold choice can materially distort graph measures and group comparisons
relevance_to_current_claim: Any topology finding requires a prespecified threshold strategy and robustness curve
limitations: No single thresholding strategy resolves every network-construction bias

title: Test-retest reproducibility of the structural connectome over multiple parcellation scales
main finding: Reproducibility differs by parcellation scale, edge weight and metric
relevance_to_current_claim: Edge and graph conclusions should be tested across construction choices
limitations: Healthy repeat scans do not capture disease-specific motion or atrophy

title: Network diffusion model of progression predicts longitudinal patterns of atrophy and metabolism in Alzheimer's disease
modality: structural MRI, FDG PET and normative connectome
main finding: Baseline network-diffusion predictions tracked later atrophy and hypometabolism patterns
relevance_to_current_claim: Longitudinal network-spread prediction is established prior art
limitations: Uses a template connectome and population-level patterns rather than subject-specific tract injury

title: The challenge of mapping the human connectome based on diffusion tractography
cohort: 96 international tractography pipelines on a realistic phantom
main finding: Most pipelines produced many false-positive bundles and no method solved sensitivity-specificity tradeoffs
relevance_to_current_claim: Strong caution against treating all detected edges as anatomical truth
limitations: Phantom anatomy and signal cannot reproduce every in-vivo disease effect

title: Investigating white matter fibre density and morphology using fixel-based analysis
main finding: Fixel metrics permit fiber-specific inference in crossing-fiber voxels
relevance_to_current_claim: FBA is established and can strengthen specificity beyond voxelwise FA
limitations: Biological interpretation still depends on acquisition, modeling and registration

title: Harmonization of multi-site diffusion tensor imaging data
main finding: ComBat removed scanner effects while preserving biological covariates in regional DTI measures
relevance_to_current_claim: Site harmonization is required for pooled diagnostic analyses
limitations: Basic ComBat assumes specified covariates and may not handle nonlinear or spatially complex scanner effects

title: Structural tract alterations predict downstream tau accumulation in amyloid-positive older individuals
cohort: amyloid-positive older adults with longitudinal tau PET
modality: dMRI, amyloid PET, tau PET and cognition
main finding: Higher diffusivity in hippocampal output tracts predicted later connected-neocortical tau accumulation and memory decline
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for a generic limbic-tract-to-tau-to-memory mechanism
limitations: Modest cohort and observational mediation cannot prove trans-neuronal spread

title: Limits to anatomical accuracy of diffusion tractography using modern approaches
main finding: Modern algorithms remained limited by false positives and incomplete recovery of known pathways
relevance_to_current_claim: Pipeline sophistication does not eliminate anatomical uncertainty
limitations: Nonhuman validation and specific acquisition protocols

title: MRtrix3: A fast, flexible and open software framework for medical image processing and visualisation
main finding: Documented the widely used open-source implementation for CSD, tractography and connectomics
relevance_to_current_claim: Using MRtrix3 is implementation provenance, not novelty
limitations: Software flexibility increases the need to report every parameter and version

title: Connectomes from streamlines tractography: Assigning streamlines to brain parcellations is not trivial but highly consequential
cohort: in-house and Human Connectome Project data
main finding: Minor assignment changes altered pairwise connectivity, modules and graph metrics
relevance_to_current_claim: Node-assignment and construction sensitivity are central to biological claims
limitations: No single assignment solution guarantees anatomical ground truth

title: Graph convolutional neural networks for Alzheimer's disease classification
journal: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
main finding: A graph neural network classified AD-related groups using structural-connectome topology
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for a generic GNN-on-DTI-connectome claim
limitations: Conference-scale study with limited external validation and interpretability

title: Explainable Brain Disease Classification and Relevance-Guided Deep Learning
journal: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research: MIDL
main finding: Connectome-specific deep learning produced diagnoses and edge-level relevance maps
relevance_to_current_claim: Explainable connectome classification is established
limitations: Saliency is not causal and validation was dataset-limited

title: Longitudinal predictive modeling of tau progression along the structural connectome
main finding: Structural-connectome-constrained models predicted longitudinal regional tau progression
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct prior art for connectome-based tau-spread prediction
limitations: Model predictions depend on the connectome template or estimation and assumed diffusion dynamics

title: Deep fusion of brain structure-function in mild cognitive impairment
main finding: Joint connectivity representations improved MCI classification over single modalities
relevance_to_current_claim: Multimodal deep fusion is established
limitations: Classification performance does not itself reveal disease mechanism; external transportability limited

title: Whole-brain modeling of the differential influences of amyloid-beta and tau in Alzheimer's disease
modality: MRI, amyloid PET, tau PET and connectome-informed simulation
main finding: The fitted model suggested greater amyloid influence in MCI and greater tau influence in AD on excitation-inhibition dynamics
relevance_to_current_claim: A generic whole-brain mechanistic-network framing is already occupied
limitations: Model identifiability and causal interpretation remain challenging

title: Alzheimer's Disease Prediction via Brain Structural-Functional Deep Fusing Network
journal: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
main finding: CT-GAN fused structural and functional connectivity for AD-stage prediction and highlighted influential connections
relevance_to_current_claim: Transformers and cross-modal imaging fusion are established
limitations: Generative fidelity and internal diagnostic accuracy do not establish biological novelty

title: Information leakage inflates prediction performance in connectome-based machine learning
methods: leakage experiments across preprocessing and cross-validation
main finding: Data leakage can markedly inflate connectome prediction performance
relevance_to_current_claim: All preprocessing, feature selection, harmonization and tuning must occur within subject-level training folds
limitations: Exact leakage modes differ across datasets and pipelines

title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network with Transformer-Guided Adaptive Diffusion for Preclinical Alzheimer Classification
journal: Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention
modality: white-matter connectome, structural MRI and PET-derived features
methods: graph neural network with transformer-guided adaptive diffusion
main finding: Short- and long-range graph information from multiple modalities improved preclinical AD classification and highlighted candidate ROIs
relevance_to_current_claim: Direct novelty killer for a generic multimodal GNN-transformer claim
limitations: Conference study and limited evidence of external clinical transportability

title: Synaptic loss pattern is constrained by brain connectome and modulated by phosphorylated tau in Alzheimer's disease
modality: SV2A PET, amyloid PET, plasma p-tau and normative connectome
main finding: Synaptic loss patterns were partially constrained by network topology and modulated by p-tau181
relevance_to_current_claim: Connectome-constrained downstream injury is already demonstrated beyond dMRI
limitations: Mostly normative functional connectivity, only 18 longitudinal cases and observational inference
